Key audit matter:
Valuation of unquoted equity investments
The Group holds significant unquoted equity investments measured
at fair value through profit or loss and at fair value through other
comprehensive income.
As explained under Note 17 of the financial statements, the Group
uses a variety of approaches in estimating the fair value of these
investments. The methods used in determining the fair value of the
unquoted investments involve significant estimates and assumptions
of unobservable inputs such as comparable market multiples,
appropriate discounting rates and incorporation of illiquidity
discounts.
Changes in these assumptions could result in material variations to
the carrying amounts of the investments in the statement of financial
position and the recorded gains/losses in the statement of profit or
loss, and statement of other comprehensive income.
How our audit addressed the key audit ma:
We assessed management’s processes and controls for determination
of the fair values of investments.
We assessed the valuation method used and the underlying
assumptions such as the selected comparable entities, liquidity
discounts, and any other adjustments.
We tested the accuracy of the computations.
We evaluated the adequacy and appropriateness of disclosures in
the financial statements.
